papers.title: The LLM-Attacker: A Unified Red-Team Framework for Privacy Evaluation of Split and Distributed LLM Systems
papers.problem: Teams cannot compare privacy tests for split language models because each test uses different attacker access, data, and scoring.
papers.fix: LLM-Attacker records every test choice; in one GPT-2 test, extra training gradients raised exact-document recovery from 13.71% to 37.77%.
papers.practicalUseCase: Privacy claims mean little without context, so name the attacker, data, and scoring rule in every claim.
papers.limitation: The main experiment uses GPT-2 only and is shared with a companion study.

papers.title: EvalResearchBench: Can AI Agents Build Their Own Feedback for Recursive Self-Improvement?
papers.problem: Rerunning full benchmarks costs too much, so experts hand-pick smaller test sets to save money.
papers.fix: The best AI-built test suites ranked about 75% of model pairs the same way the real benchmarks did.
papers.practicalUseCase: Agent-built tests are not yet reliable, so keep a human-picked sample of public tasks as your baseline.
papers.limitation: Agent-built tests can cut off answers, run out of budget, or let a few questions dominate a score.

papers.title: Diffusion Language Models Change Speed Across Tasks and Languages
papers.problem: Two diffusion model outputs of equal length can cost very different amounts, and the reasons were unclear.
papers.fix: Story writing took more than three times the passes per token that grammar correction took.
papers.practicalUseCase: Expect copy-and-edit jobs to run cheap; weighting answers by decoding speed beat majority voting by up to 4.2 points.
papers.limitation: The study covers only two diffusion models across 10 tasks.

papers.title: Different Tasks, Different Timesteps: Temporal Task-Aware Quantization for Diffusion Language Models
papers.problem: Shrinking diffusion language models loses accuracy because each task needs different precision at different denoising steps.
papers.fix: T2Quant sets precision per step with a label-free signal, raising accuracy up to 6.7 percentage points at equal budget.
papers.practicalUseCase: When you compress these models, tune precision by task and step instead of using one setting everywhere.
papers.limitation: Tests covered three diffusion models and six benchmarks, so other models may behave differently.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks set up sustainability committees, but nobody knew whether they change environmental results in dual banking systems.
papers.fix: Committees raised all four environmental measures overall, but in Islamic banks they lifted only overall and resource scores.
papers.practicalUseCase: Islamic bank committees may show symbolic effort, so judge them on green products and innovations, not on their existence.
papers.limitation: Panel regressions show links between committees and scores, not proof of cause.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Little was known about how sustainability sukuk issuance grew or what sets the size of each issue.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk issues, sustainability sukuk stayed tiny, and equity-based contracts gave larger issues than sale-based ones.
papers.practicalUseCase: Issuers wanting bigger issues should favour equity-based contracts and watch second party opinion costs, which shrink issue size.
papers.limitation: The data end in 2022, and growth sits mostly in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Saudi Arabia.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Nobody had shown whether AI and big data help Islamic banks in Jordan compete and develop sustainably.
papers.fix: AI use, big data skills, and data management all raised competitiveness and sustainability; staff digital skill raised only competitiveness.
papers.practicalUseCase: Invest in AI, analytics, and data management first, because staff digital skill alone did not lift sustainability.
papers.limitation: One survey of 214 managers at Jordanian Islamic banks shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Little evidence showed what drives bank growth in countries that run both Islamic and conventional banks.
papers.fix: Across 218 banks in 12 countries, ICT adoption drove expansion most, and high-tech exports helped only when combined with ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: Banks should put digital infrastructure first, and Islamic banks also need strong governance to grow.
papers.limitation: Data cover 218 banks in 12 countries from 2010 to 2023, so other markets may differ.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Many people in Muslim-majority countries still lack financial services, even after a decade of Islamic finance growth.
papers.fix: Across 35 countries, income, education, institutional quality, and internet access drove financial inclusion in OIC states.
papers.practicalUseCase: OIC countries should invest in digital infrastructure, youth and women empowerment, and income growth, unlike OECD countries.
papers.limitation: Data cover only 35 OIC and OECD countries from 2005 to 2021.

papers.title: Exploring the influencing factors of academic doctoral students’ academic innovation behavior in the context of generative artificial intelligence: Self-determination theory and motivation-opportunity-ability perspectives
papers.problem: Generative AI helps and harms doctoral students, so what drives their academic innovation was unclear.
papers.fix: Intrinsic and extrinsic motivation drive innovation together, and long-term unmet needs sharply cut flexibility and willingness to explore.
papers.practicalUseCase: Support doctoral students' basic needs, because strong resources can partly cover for weak motivation.
papers.limitation: One-time self-reported survey data cannot prove cause, and reverse causality is possible.
